critical_code_review_comments: Duplicate data-testid="ambient-sound-toggle" — Header.jsx renders <AmbientSoundToggle> twice (once in desktop nav, once in mobile actions cluster). Both nodes carry the same testid, so `page.locator('[data-testid=ambient-sound-toggle]').first` picks whichever comes first in DOM (currently the desktop one, hidden via `md:flex` ancestor at mobile widths). This forces test authors to use `:visible` filter. Consider distinct testids: `ambient-sound-toggle-desktop` / `ambient-sound-toggle-mobile`.
Header.jsx line ~87 still has dead status-pill div (`hidden items-center gap-2.5 md:hidden`) noted in iteration 2 — carried over.

AmbientSoundToggle keeps its AudioContext alive after user turns sound OFF (only master.gain ramps to 0, oscillators + LFO keep running). Fine for UX/battery in most cases, but if the toggle unmounts without turning off first, `useEffect` cleanup closes ctx — OK. Consider suspending ctx after fade-out completes to save CPU when off.
SmoothScroll.jsx exposes `window.__lenis` globally as an implicit API for the whole app. Tests rely on this. Acceptable, but document it (or expose via React context) to keep discoverability high.

Lenis prints console warning: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative, fixed, or absolute…'. Harmless but noisy — set `position: relative` on html/body or pass a `wrapper`/`content` prop to Lenis constructor to silence.

Carry-over from iteration 1: ContactSection uses <input type=email> whose native browser validation short-circuits React onSubmit, making [data-testid=contact-error] path for invalid emails unreachable in tests.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 clean on live URL https://mind-nexus-dark.preview.emergentagent.com. Note when testing ambient toggle: two DOM nodes share data-testid="ambient-sound-toggle" (desktop nav + mobile cluster), one is display:none per viewport — use ':visible' selector or nth. For 5-block cross-fade, ProblemSection uses useScroll offset ['start start','end end'] so map scrollYProgress p to window.scrollY via y = section.top + p*(section.height - viewport.height). Chromium blocks AudioContext auto-start until user gesture — click satisfies this; graph is created on first tap and reused thereafter. window.__lenis exposes {scrollTo, stop, start} used by Header/Hero/brand-logo.
